newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ministers silent on rate rise to aid yen-EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan ministers silent on rate rise to aid yen-EPA.

text.p: Japanese ministers did not comment at this morning's cabinet meeting when the issue was raised of whether Japan should increase interest rates to cope with excessive weakening of the yen against the dollar, Japan's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Minister Taro Aso told a news conference on Friday.
Asked whether any of the cabinet ministers made comments that Japan should raise interest rates in response to the yen's weakening, Aso said, "No, there weren't any."

The topic of interest rate differentials between the United States and Japan was also mentioned at the cabinet meeting, although no comments were made in reference to policy measures to address the gap, Aso said.

Although Management and Coordination Agency Director-General Kabun Muto during a cabinet meeting on Tuesday urged the Bank of Japan to consider raising the official discount rate, there were no further comments today that Japan should alter its interest rate policy, Aso said.

Aso also said that Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka at this morning's cabinet meeting reiterated comments made at Thursday's bankers' conference that excessive weakening of the yen as well as excessive strength of the yen were unfavourable and that Japan would act decisively against such movements.
